summary: API gateway load swell leading to upstream runtime panic and sustained 5xx for enterprise tenant
description: Issue summary: Starting ~2026-03-13T14:12 UTC BrightRetail (enterprise tenant) reported elevated 5xx rates for chat and embeddings routes. Errors observed primarily from API gateway returning 502/503 and a correlated increase in upstream runtime restarts (SIGTERM/SIGABRT) and NVML driver resets on a subset of dedicated runtimes.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Replay customer traffic pattern: steady small-embedding batches (<=8 items) mixed with chat requests at ~1200 rps total
2) Use us-west tenant routing with model pinning to open-chat-v2-0618 and embed-small-quant2
3) Observe api-gateway accept queue growth and hedged retries; watch upstream runtime logs for driver resets and process exits
logs: 2026-03-13T14:17:10Z runtime[slot-7] ERROR nvml: GPU driver reset detected; pid=21845 trace=...
2026-03-13T14:17:13Z runtime[slot-7] FATAL signal=SIGABRT plugin:kv_cache.cpp:421 assertion failed
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: sudden small-batch embedding fanout + priority hedged retries caused accept-queue saturation on api-gateway proxies, which amplified load to a subset of runtimes pinned for the tenant.

Metric correlation: pod restart count for runtimes in shard us-west-2a rose from baseline 0.02/hr to 6/hr between 14:10-14:25 UTC. API gateway 5xx rate jumped from 0.3% to 18% for tenant BrightRetail.
Trace sample: request-id=brt-14k-9f shows api-gateway issued hedged retry after 400ms, second attempt hit the same runtime replica which was in pre-crash state (OOM-on-kv-replay).
Observed NVML resets on two GPUs belonging to the same fault domain; kernel logs show repeated iowait on NVMe during heavy kv_cache writes and prefetch traffic.

Reproduced locally in staging with synthetic replay at 50% of production rps when forcing small-embed batching and disabling prefix cache: runtime memory grew steadily and leaked host pinned allocations leading to final driver reset.

Temporary mitigation applied: rate-limit tenant embedding concurrency to 60 concurrent embeddings and disabled hedged-retry for embedding route for us-west region. This reduced 5xx from ~18% to ~2.1% within 6 minutes.
comments: Elena Park (2026-03-13T14:28): Customer reports degraded responses in their production application. Attached sample customer request IDs and approximate timestamps.
Miguel Santos (2026-03-13T14:35): Investigating; adding SRE on-call and will attempt targeted restart of affected runtime pool. Increasing proxy accept_queue temporarily.
SRE Oncall - Priya Rao (2026-03-13T14:42): Performed rolling restart of runtime shard us-west-2a. Noticed one node with nvme iowait spikes coincident with GPU resets. Isolating that host.

Eng - Tomas Becker (2026-03-13T15:05): Heap analysis from local repro indicates a kv_cache path holding host buffers during high prefetch churn. Creating a runtime patch to add stricter prefetch backpressure and guard allocations.

Customer Rep - Jordan Miles (BrightRetail) (2026-03-13T15:20): Confirmed visible improvement after rate-limits. Asking for ETA on full fix and whether traffic will be automatically rerouted if issue recurs.
resolution: Applied short-term mitigations: tenant-level concurrency cap on embeddings, disabled hedged retries on embed routes in us-west, isolated and decommissioned one faulty host with nvme hot path. Rolled a runtime hotfix (serving-runtime PR #4821) to add backpressure on prefetch and to fail fast on excessive host buffer growth. Monitored for 24 hours; 5xx baseline returned to <0.5% and customer reported normal behavior.
follow_up_actions: 1) Deploy runtime patch in all us-west runtime pools during low-traffic window (ENG-ROLL-2026-03-15).
2) Adjust autoscaler thresholds to prefer node addition earlier on accept_queue > 300 for edge proxies (OPS-1458).
3) Add dashboard alert for NVMe iowait correlated with GPU resets and link to runtime restart counts.
4) Update canary traffic policy to avoid hedged retries hitting same replica (API-GW-RET-23).
5) Provide customer-facing incident summary and postmortem within 48 hours; schedule follow-up call with BrightRetail engineering lead.
